gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Tesla's own Gen 3 Wall Connector spec caps output at 12–48 A, so at a Gen 3 destination charger the 80 A (Lectron, A2Z) and 60 A continuous (TeslaTap Mini) ratings ChatGPT used to rank the adapters all deliver the same 48 A at most. Ratings that do differ once normalised are A2Z's IP54 when plugged in (its IP67 applies only unplugged), its published CSA certificate number and 24-month warranty, set against Lectron's unqualified IP67 with no certificate number and $29 lower price.
standout_why: I could not open either cited thisWATT page (guide and TeslaTap spec page) because of a self-signed certificate error, so I can't rule out that they have this. ChatGPT's two answers do not mention a 48 A charger cap. Instead they treat 80 A as 'extra headroom' and rank on amps. I also read two uncited top results. evandcharger.com says only that 'the highest hardwired residential units stop at 48 A or 50 A' and advises preferring 80 A on a 48 A charger 'because it runs cooler'. electrifiedexperts.com says the car's onboard charger caps current. Neither cites Tesla's Gen 3 spec, says whether ratings are continuous or maximum, or separates IP ratings plugged in from unplugged. Neither gives A2Z's CSA certificate number. The cited a2zev.com page has the IP54 and certificate figures, but no rival lines them up against Lectron.
decides: This confirms the Lectron 80A UL 2252 as the value pick at $129.99 today, $20 below the $149.99 ChatGPT showed. At a Gen 3 Wall Connector its 80 A buys no speed over a 60 A TeslaTap, and it carries a UL 2252 claim and a temperature sensor that TeslaTap's page does not. The A2Z Stellar costs $159.00 today, not the $111.42 ChatGPT showed. The extra $29.01 buys documentation, not speed: a CSA certificate number, a disclosed IP54 rating when plugged in, dual over-temperature switches, a dual lock and a 24-month warranty. The TeslaTap Mini 60A at $194.96 and 80A at $224.96 cost $65–95 more than the Lectron. Their maker pages state no listing and no temperature monitoring, and the extra amps can't be used on a Gen 3 unit. The older Lectron 48A is listed as 'SGS certified under the UL 2251 standard', which is the connector standard, not the UL 2252 adapter standard.
